feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Evidence from earlier iterations: iteration 6 (0.5 kg, 0.10 m track, 7 sensors at +/-0.06 m, 16 mm footprints, lead 0.05 m) is the best design at 586.9. Its slalom progress is 0.39 with line loss 0.05 and max_error 0.0618, so it still ends at the 0.06 m floor. Its oval finish is 0.90 and s-bend finish 0.65, with s-bend oscillation 0.518. Iteration 5 (+/-0.07 m reach) cut slalom progress to 0.15, so reach is not the slalom limit. Iteration 4 (0.08 m track) overshot, with s-bend oscillation 0.45, so turn authority is not the limit either. The integration work for this candidate is to keep the iteration-6 controller unchanged, so that the footprint change is read alone. The sensor weights stay proportional to sensor x at the iteration-6 span. The main risk I am handling is edge-crossing jitter with a smaller footprint. Interpret the next race as follows. If slalom progress rises above 0.39 or a slalom finish appears, and s-bend steering_oscillation stays below about 0.55, keep 12 mm and move to the mass change in the requests below. If s-bend oscillation rises above about 0.55 while the slalom does not improve, revert to 16 mm, because the sharper footprint is adding jitter. If the slalom is unchanged with max_error still at about 0.06 m, the footprint is not the limit, so keep the geometry and let the Integrator adjust kd or base_speed.
requested_changes: If slalom progress rises above 0.39 or finishes appear while s-bend steering_oscillation stays below about 0.55, keep sensor_size 0.012 m and hold mass at 0.5 kg, since iteration 6 showed that 0.5 kg gave the slalom its only gain (0.34 to 0.39).

If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above about 0.55 (iteration 6: 0.518) with no slalom gain, return sensor_size to 0.016 m and keep mass at 0.5 kg with the iteration-6 layout, since the smaller footprint is adding edge jitter and iteration 6 is the best tested design.

If the slalom max_error stays at about 0.06 m with line loss near 0.05 after the footprint change, do not make another geometry change; hold the iteration-6 geometry and report the result, since iteration 5 showed that reach and track changes do not help the slalom and the remaining limit is the controller's kd or base_speed.
